rationale: Three identifier spaces hit the same race in three days: lesson IDs nearly double-allocated (local next_id:L034 vs upstream-landed L034), ADR numbers duplicated (two 0002s, two 0003s, two 0005s), and Track A/B phase ranges overlap; the wiring-era L035-L038 mints were superseded by different content under the same IDs after fork reconciliation, proving the race bit rather than merely threatened.

lesson.title: Reconcile monotonic identifiers against merged history before allocating them
lesson.source: fleet muster 2026-08-26 (metis): vault next_id raced upstream L034 (0052), ADR numbers duplicated (volt-comm drift #3, W0 dedupe), roadmap phase ranges collide
lesson.lesson: Before allocating any monotonic identifier - lesson IDs, ADR numbers, phase numbers, release numbers - fetch and scan the authoritative merged history for existing use; a counter read from a local copy is a hypothesis whenever copies can diverge. On collision, renumber with documented cross-reference updates (bracket notes, annotated log entries), never silent rewrite; when two copies already assigned one ID to different content, treat reconciliation as a data-integrity incident, not a formatting chore.
